question: Explain how type 2 diabetes can result in persistently high blood glucose concentrations.
answer: Target cells have fewer or less responsive insulin receptors, so glucose uptake is reduced and the beta cells may stop producing enough insulin
mark_scheme: MP1 1 mark: Target cells less responsive to insulin or fewer receptors. Accept: less responsive; not responsive; insulin resistance; resistant to insulin; fewer insulin receptors; fewer receptors. MP2 1 mark: Less glucose uptake so blood glucose stays high. Accept: less glucose uptake; less glucose is taken up; glucose is not taken up; glucose uptake reduced; reduced glucose uptake; fewer glucose transporters. Allow any wording that conveys the idea, including common alternatives, correct hedged answers ('I think ...') and clearly intended spelling. Ignore extra correct detail. No mark if the idea is negated, contradicted, or the response gives two different answers.
model_answer: In type 2 diabetes the body cells become less responsive to insulin because receptors are lost or are less sensitive; fewer glucose transporters move to the membrane, so glucose uptake and conversion to glycogen are reduced and blood glucose stays high.
common_misconceptions: Students say that type 2 diabetes is caused by lack of insulin production from birth.
